A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the palaeolatitude (PL) of Baltica is ∼ 30°, which is consistent with a position at 45°N in the Pangean reconstruction by Torsvik et al. (2001) (Figure 1).
the Lunner dykes were emplaced ∼271 ± 2 Ma ago, at a palaeolatitude for the Oslo Graben of ∼ 20°.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the palaeolatitudes of Baltica are not significantly different from those of Pangea B (the Pangea configuration after the closure of the Rheic Ocean).
the Lunner dyke swarm is ∼30 Ma older than previously assumed, but that it is also ∼30 m.y. younger than the Oslo Rift dykes.
